clue.text: Spice Girl's bit of leopard print clothing radical? Originally, yes

definitions.note: the clue's 's reads as 'is', so the definition is a Spice Girl

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the spot is put round the next letter

parts.note: a spot is one mark of a leopard-print pattern

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word radical

parts.note: Y is the short form of yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: A pop star's leopard-print outfit is asked whether it is daring, and the reply is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts SPOT round R, the first letter of 'radical' ('Originally'); Y for yes finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporty Spice was the nickname of Melanie Chisholm in the 1990s pop group.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer after Home Secretary's A&E mix-up

indicators.note: an A and E mix-up means those two letters swap places

parts.note: Priti Patel was the UK Home Secretary when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A minister's blunder after a muddle at a hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower. A&E is a British hospital's accident and emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one part of a flower, and a bloomer is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Turns on the radio leading to theatre jobs

indicators.note: on the radio, words are heard, not seen, so this signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: turns, as a ball rolls over

explanation.surface: Turns on the radio, which leads to work in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns on' looks like switching on; 'Turns' gives ROLLS and 'on the radio' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Roles are the parts actors play in a theatre production.

clue.text: Y-fronts of yuppies threaten to rip if unwisely manspread

definitions.note: Y is the chemical symbol for this element

indicators.note: fronts of means the opening letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: A yuppie's underpants are close to splitting when he sits with legs splayed.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are British men's briefs; here the hyphen splits Y, the definition, from 'fronts of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Y is the chemical symbol of yttrium, a rare-earth metal.

clue.text: "Eh up!", pants Spice Girl appearing halfway through Glee

indicators.note: pants as a verb looks like breathless speech, but here it says the letters of Eh up are jumbled, as if the words were mixed up
halfway through means only the back half of the name is kept, its first half dropped

parts.note: Victoria Beckham (Posh Spice) is a Spice Girl

explanation.surface: A northerner gasps 'Eh up!' as a pop star turns up in the middle of the TV show Glee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' turns EHUP into EUPH; 'halfway through' leaves ORIA, the second half of VICTORIA. 'Eh up' is a northern English greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is intense happiness, a close synonym of glee.

clue.text: European gesture shows passion

parts.note: a motion of the hand is a gesture

explanation.surface: A continental's hand movement reveals strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is a strong feeling, and so an emotion.

clue.text: Somewhat cheap, a god asks for temples

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deity asks a worshipper for cheap temples.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagodas are tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple towers in Asia.

clue.text: One may go white when questioned about poison

definitions.text: One may go white when questioned about poison

parts.words: One may go white when questioned about poison
parts.note: 'What's your poison?' is slang for 'what will you drink?', and a wine lover might choose white

explanation.surface: Someone turns pale when interrogated over a poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go white' looks like turning pale with fear; it is choosing white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a connoisseur of wine, so someone choosing red or white.

clue.text: During outrageous scenes, get naked at bottom

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: outrageous means wild, so the letters of scenes are thrown about
naked means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: In wild scenes, people get naked from the waist down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges SCENES into ESSENC; 'naked' strips 'get' to E.
explanation.definitionFit: At bottom means fundamentally, the same idiom as in essence.

clue.text: Disease from Congress allowed to spike

parts.note: congress here is sexual intercourse, so the disease is an STI, a sexually transmitted infection
allowed means let

explanation.surface: A politician picks up an illness in Congress and is allowed to suffer a spike in symptoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature; it is the old word for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a spike heel on a shoe, or a thin pointed dagger.

clue.text: Some girl's name describing one short Spice Girl

definitions.text: Some girl's name describing one short Spice Girl

indicators.note: some of a word means just a piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was a Spice Girl

explanation.surface: A girl's nickname that labels one particular member of the pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines Ginger Spice, Geri Halliwell; 'describing' just links the letters, and 'short' trims GERI to GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Spice was Geri Halliwell's nickname in the group, a name given for her red hair.

clue.text: CIA's files reviewed and ultimately marked confidential

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again in a new order, so the letters of the CIA's files are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word marked

explanation.surface: Intelligence files are reviewed and finally stamped as confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' reworks CIASFILES and 'ultimately' adds D, the last letter of 'marked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are officially secret, restricted to authorised readers.

clue.text: Hot scoops regularly knocked back Spice Girl

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink thrown back, says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word scoops

explanation.surface: Scoops of something hot are regularly downed by a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes SOP from 'scoops'; 'knocked back' reverses HSOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh Spice was Victoria Beckham's nickname in the 1990s girl group.

clue.text: Aristos glower when interrupted by Spice Girl in retirement

indicators.note: retirement is going back, so the whole construction is read backwards
interrupted by means the other piece breaks into the middle of this one

parts.note: read as glow-er, a thing that glows, such as a neon light
Mel B (Melanie Brown) was a Spice Girl

explanation.surface: Aristocrats scowl when a retired pop star barges in on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glower' is not a scowl but a thing that glows: NEON. 'interrupted by' makes NE-MELB-ON, and 'in retirement' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristos is short for aristocrats, members of the titled nobility.

clue.text: Patron of the arts cutting fancy rope — time to get to work

indicators.note: cutting means the inner pieces slice into the middle of the jumbled word
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters of rope are rearranged

parts.note: an era is a period of time
go means to set to work, as in 'go for it'

explanation.surface: An arts sponsor slices through ornate rope, as it is time to start work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' gives OPER, which 'cutting' splits after its second letter. 'Patron' suggests a sponsor, but here it is simply a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera-goer is a regular audience member, a patron in the sense of a customer.

clue.text: Numberless aches following long jump when Olympics are held

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a leap is a long jump

indicators.note: numberless means losing the letter that abbreviates number

parts.note: to ache for is to yearn, so aches means yearns

explanation.surface: Countless aches after the long jump at the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numberless' removes N, the abbreviation for number, from YEARNS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Summer Olympics usually fall in a leap year, the four-yearly year with an extra day.

clue.text: Coming down rapidly, thousands flee Reading in haste

indicators.note: the thousands flee, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: skimming is reading quickly
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them are MM

explanation.surface: A rapid descent sends thousands running from the town of Reading in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the English town; it is reading a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing is sliding down snowy slopes at speed on skis.

clue.text: State secrecy provision covers dictator's wife

indicators.note: covers means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: an NDA is a non-disclosure agreement, a contract enforcing secrecy
Eva Braun married Hitler; Eva Perón was the wife of Argentina's Juan Perón

explanation.surface: A government gagging order protects a dictator's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' at the front looks like a verb meaning declare; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the United States, home of Las Vegas.

clue.text: Shunning red, Chelsea ran around their rivals

indicators.note: shunning means the red's letters are left out of the pool
around means the remaining letters are moved round into a new order

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous red, a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: Avoiding a red card, Chelsea's team ran rings around their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CHELSEA RAN, remove CHE, and rearrange what is left. Chelsea and Arsenal are rival London football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal are Chelsea's long-standing London football rivals, so 'their' refers back to Chelsea.

clue.text: Writer's block starting — editor is discouraged

indicators.note: starting means the block comes first, ahead of the writer

parts.note: a dam blocks a river
a pen is a writer, the thing that writes

explanation.surface: An author's writer's block sets in and the editor loses heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' reads as one familiar phrase, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'starting' puts the block first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampened spirits are lowered ones, so dampened means discouraged.

clue.text: Cover's upset Spice Girl — it's problematic

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: a dilemma is something problematic

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a lid is a cover, with the 's read as 'is'
Emma Bunton (Baby Spice) was a Spice Girl

explanation.surface: A cover version has upset a pop star, and that is a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distress; it reverses LID. 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a tricky situation with no good choice, a thing that is problematic.

clue.text: Spice Girl goes over old hit, occasionally sounding tuneful

indicators.note: goes over means the singer's name stretches over, around, the other letters

parts.note: Mel C (Melanie Chisholm) was a Spice Girl

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A singer covers an old hit, sometimes sounding in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'goes over' means sits around; Mel C is Sporty Spice, Melanie Chisholm.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic means having a pleasing tune, so it describes something that sounds tuneful.

clue.text: Spice Girl starts to booze aboard Becks' yacht

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: A pop star starts drinking on David Beckham's yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: Becks is David Beckham, footballer and husband of Posh Spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby Spice was Emma Bunton's nickname in the girl group.

clue.text: For others' benefit, saloon's opening without Sprite?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an elf is a sprite, so a made-up adverb for lacking one is elflessly, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A bar's launch goes ahead without a famous fizzy drink, for the good of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprite' looks like the lemonade brand; it is an elf. The question mark flags the invented word ELFLESSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting selflessly means putting other people's interests before your own.

clue.text: Spice Girl's a little sad about track

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is a Spice Girl

indicators.note: a little of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ca is short for the Latin circa, about
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A pop star is a bit down over a song track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' suggests a song; it is a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Scary Spice was Mel B's nickname in the 1990s pop group.

clue.text: Deceived duke trapped in Spanish province

indicators.note: trapped in means the first letter is held inside the province

parts.note: León is a province in northern Spain

explanation.surface: A tricked nobleman is stuck in a region of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' puts D inside LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to mislead them, so being deceived is being led on.

clue.text: Complete postgrad degree covering empire

parts.note: to do a course is to complete it
an MA is a Master of Arts, a postgraduate degree
in, as in 'a degree in history', means covering a subject

explanation.surface: Finishing a master's that covers the history of an empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' looks like a containment signal, but nothing goes inside anything; it means 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory under one ruler, or a field of control, as an empire is.

clue.text: Ozzy Osbourne's home taking LSD in mad cocktail

definitions.note: Ozzy Osbourne came from Birmingham, in the West Midlands

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: The rock star's house where people take acid in a wild drug mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Ozzy Osbourne, Black Sabbath's singer, grew up in Aston, Birmingham; the Midlands is central England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midlands is the central region of England, where the singer was born and raised.

clue.text: City supporters having trouble getting back after international

indicators.note: after means the reversed trouble comes behind the international

parts.note: bras are supporters, items of underwear

indicators.note: getting back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to ail is to be in trouble or unwell

explanation.surface: Fans of a city club struggle to make a comeback after an international fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' reverses AIL to LIA. 'supporters' looks like football fans; they are bras.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the capital city of Brazil.

clue.text: Charlie replaces Snoopy's lead in tears

indicators.note: replaces means one letter comes in where another stood
lead means the first letter of the word is the one changed

parts.note: a snoopy person is prying, nosy
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie Brown's dog Snoopy loses his leadership role and is in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snoopy' and 'Charlie' suggest the Peanuts cartoon, but snoopy here is just nosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying means weeping, shedding tears.
